findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting row is missing or doesn't match a category
findings.body: The migration computes the category id via `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories c INNER JOIN site_settings s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. site_settings rows only exist for settings an admin actually changed, so on any site that never set embed_category (or left it blank, or where the value doesn't exactly equal a category name) the query returns zero rows, `execute(...)[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError (PG::Result may also raise IndexError). The migration aborts, blocking the deploy — this will hit most existing sites since embedding is off by default, and fresh installs where site_settings is empty. The same unguarded `[0]['value']` pattern is used for uncategorized_category_id on line 15. Check for an empty result before indexing and fall back to the uncategorized category.

findings.title: Migration interpolates legacy host strings directly into raw SQL
findings.body: Legacy hosts are inserted with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. Any host value containing a single quote (e.g. an apostrophe someone pasted into the old free-text setting) produces malformed SQL and aborts the migration mid-run, and it is an injection vector. Use bound parameters or `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` when building the INSERT.

findings.title: Migrated hosts keep http(s):// prefix and paths, so they silently stop matching
findings.body: The old SiteSetting-based allowlist explicitly accepted entries like `http://eviltrout.com` (the removed code and its specs stripped the scheme before comparing), so real sites can have scheme-prefixed or path-bearing entries in the `embeddable_hosts` setting. The migration copies those values verbatim into the new table, but the new lookup `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares the stored value against the parsed hostname (`where("lower(host) = ?", host)`), and the model's scheme/path stripping lives in `before_validation`, which raw SQL inserts bypass. After upgrading, rows like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` never match, so comment embedding and feed import from those previously-working sites break without any error. Normalize the values (strip scheme and path, downcase) in the migration, mirroring the model's before_validation.

findings.title: update and destroy 500 on a nonexistent host id instead of 404
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` fetch the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then use it without a nil check: `save_host(host)` immediately does `host.host = ...` and `destroy` calls `host.destroy`. If the id doesn't exist — e.g. an admin saves or deletes a row that another admin already removed in a different tab — this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 with no meaningful feedback instead of a 404. Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` (which renders 404 via rescuing RecordNotFound) or explicitly handle the nil case.

findings.title: New admin endpoints have no request specs — only a subclass assertion
findings.body: Both new controller specs (`admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`) only assert the controller is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. The feature's server API — creating, updating and deleting hosts, the uncategorized-category defaulting, validation-error responses for malformed hosts, and staff/admin permission enforcement — has no request coverage, so regressions (including the nil-host 500s in update/destroy) won't be caught. Add request specs exercising create/update/destroy with valid and invalid input and with non-admin users.

findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!` twice unconditionally. The controller assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, so a request that omits the host param leaves `self.host` nil and `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError, turning a bad request into a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if self.host.present?` or use `self.host = host.to_s.gsub(...)`, and rely on the format validation to reject blank values.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint on host — duplicates make category assignment ambiguous
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost` validates only the format of `host`, and the migration adds no unique index. The new admin UI makes it easy to add the same host twice with different categories; `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` then does `.where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, returning an arbitrary matching row, so which category embedded topics from that host land in becomes nondeterministic. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host, case_sensitive: false` and ideally a unique index.

findings.title: Fabricator files' contents are swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. The suite still passes because Fabrication registers fabricators by name regardless of file, but the file names are misleading and break the convention that a fabricator file defines the fabricator it's named after — anyone editing or searching for these will look in the wrong place. Swap the two files' contents.

findings.title: Plural branch of _hydrateEmbedded can leave undefined entries in the array
findings.body: In the new `_ids` handling of `_hydrateEmbedded`, `obj[k].map(id => _lookupSubType(...))` is assigned directly to the model without any guard, whereas the singular `_id` branch only assigns `if (hydrated)`. `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined` when an id isn't present in the root payload (e.g. a sideloaded collection filtered by permissions), so the resulting property becomes `[undefined, ...]` and any later `.get()`/iteration over it will throw. Filter the mapped results (e.g. `hydrated.compact()`/`.filter(Boolean)`) or skip assignment when any id fails to resolve, matching the singular branch's behavior.
